title: JSON

exercises.title: Serialize a struct
exercises.description: `Person { Name, Age }` with `Serialize`. Build `Person { Name: "Alice", Age: 30 }`, serialize with `serde_json::to_string`, print it.

exercises.title: Deserialize JSON
exercises.description: Deserialize `{"Name":"Bob","Age":25}` into `Person` with `Deserialize`. Print name and age separated by a space (one line: `Bob 25`).

exercises.title: serde rename
exercises.description: `User` with Rust fields `first_name`, `last_name`, `birth_year` but JSON keys `first_name`, `last_name`, `birth_year` in snake_case (use `#[serde(rename = ...)]`). Marshal John/Doe/1990 and print JSON.
hints: Use `#[serde(rename = "...")]` on each field for snake_case JSON keys. snake_case names in JSON.

exercises.title: skip_serializing_if / Option
exercises.description: Use `Option<T>` with `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` with `Option` fields: only set `server: Some("api.example.com")`, leave others `None`. Serialize so output is `{"Server":"api.example.com"}` (capital `Server` in the expected JSON).
hints: `Config { server: Some(...), port: None, debug: None }`

exercises.title: Round trip
exercises.description: `Product { id, name, price }` with Serialize+Deserialize. Marshal `{1, Laptop, 999.99}`, unmarshal into a new value, print two lines exactly: `Original: {1 Laptop 999.99}` and `Recovered: {1 Laptop 999.99}` (use the same formatting for both).

exercises.title: Nested structs
exercises.description: `Address { street, city }` and `User { name, address }` with `Serialize`. Marshal and print JSON with PascalCase JSON keys (`Street`, `City`, `Name`, `Address`) (`Street`, `City`, `Name`, `Address`).
hints: PascalCase field names match the expected PascalCase JSON keys.

exercises.title: Encode a slice
exercises.description: Serialize `Vec<Person>` with two entries to a JSON array string and print it (no extra spaces beyond what `serde_json` emits).

exercises.title: Deferred nested JSON
exercises.description: `LogEntry { level, data }` where `data` is `serde_json::Value`. Parse the sample, print `level` then `data` as compact JSON on the next line. (Object key order follows `serde_json`’s canonicalization, not the source text.)

exercises.title: Decode an array
exercises.description: Parse a JSON array of people with `serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Person>>`, then print each line as `Name Age` (one `Name Age` line per person).

theory:
## JSON in Rust

The ecosystem standard is **`serde`** for serialization traits and **`serde_json`** for JSON text.

### Encode and decode

- `serde_json::to_string` / `to_vec` — serialize to JSON text or bytes
- `serde_json::from_str` / `from_slice` — deserialize from JSON

Derive `Serialize` and `Deserialize` on your structs, or implement the traits manually for custom shapes.

### Field attributes

Use Serde’s field attributes to control JSON shape:

- `#[serde(rename = "field")]` — emit a different key name
- `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` — omit `None` fields (like “omit empty” in other ecosystems)

### Streaming

For multiple JSON values in one buffer, `serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(...).into_iter::<T>()` decodes value by value without loading one giant document into memory first.
